title: Ridgeline Pro Credit Ledger Definitions — The Commercial Account Payoff Figure
content:
**Clause.** The payoff figure of a Ridgeline Pro Credit commercial account is the account's ledger balance plus the interim late charge accrued on the past-due amount shown on the latest closed statement at the tier's monthly late payment charge percentage, counted in actual days from the statement date to the payment date on a 360-day year of twelve months, rounded to the nearest cent once on the total.

## Ledger balance

The account's ledger balance is every invoice, fee, interest charge, returned payment and credit balance refund on the account, less every payment, prompt-payment discount, tax credit, return credit, fee waiver, fee reversal and dispute credit on the account.

| Added | Taken away |
|---|---|
| Invoices | Payments |
| Fees (every fee charged: late fees, late payment charges, returned payment fees, bank card surcharges and discount recaptures) | Prompt-payment discounts |
| Interest charges | Sales tax credits |
| Returned payments | Return credits |
| Credit balance refunds | Fee waivers |
| | Fee reversals |
| | Dispute credits |

## Interim late charge

The interim late charge is the past-due amount on the latest closed statement, times the tier's monthly late payment charge percentage divided by one hundred, times twelve, times the actual days from the statement date to the payment date divided by 360. The payment date is the day the payoff payment is made.

## Worked example (hypothetical Commercial Account Net 30, 2.00 percent)

| Input | Value |
|---|---|
| Ledger balance | 12000.00 |
| Past-due amount on the latest closed statement | 5432.10 |
| Days from the statement date to the payment date | 17 |
| Interim late charge: 5432.10 times 2.00 divided by one hundred, times twelve, times 17 divided by 360 | 61.5638 |
| Payoff figure: 12000.00 plus 61.5638, rounded to the nearest cent | 12061.56 |

## Basis Q&A

**Is the interim charge rounded before it is added?** No; the payoff figure is rounded to the nearest cent once, on the total.

**Which statement is read?** The latest closed statement on the account.
